The market's response is an "overreaction," Goldman Sachs analyst Nick Cash said in reiterating his Buy rating, as the publication provided no new information on whether policymakers will implement tariffs or continue to delay commentary on tariffs.

An announcement has been expected on whether the U.S. would impose a 15% tariff on copper cathode, which would potentially start in January 2027 and then rise to 30% in 2028; while no definite decision has been made yet, equities and commodities markets have been pricing in potential tariffs, which are being slightly unwound in Thursday's trading.
As a result, Cash said the stock's sudden drop has provided investors with an attractive entry point, with Freeport
shares falling 7%-8% and copper futures trading 3%-5% lower.
